title: Round 6, stream B: THE BUILD BOARD between sectors (six offers, two picks within the bank), the six colony structures bought instead of printed by schedule, prices re-based on a ledger that found kill pay out of scale
context: The owner's note 2 of 2026-11-05 (spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-05-round-6-five-notes-design.md, stream B): 'after each round ISAO proposes 6 choices of things he can build and the user chooses 2, given enough biomass'; the proposals of 2026-10-26 (economy-plan: slightly constrained, measure with a ledger first; base-development-plan phase 1: choose the order). Measure first: before this round nothing recorded income by source.
decision: The ledger (commit 1): src/domain/economy.js books kill pay by who killed (award {src}; a ram is 'ram'), credits by category and spends by kind (spend {category}: sentry, upgrade, plasma, board); state().ledger; sectorCull(r, pay) pays its kills; browser step --ledger (FROM/TO 1..5, PAY tank|tower|'', R, BOARD=pick, TAG). The board (commit 2): src/fx/sector-run.js next(via) hands the break to storyApi.interlude with { n, via }; 'continue' (the debrief's CONTINUE) opens src/fx/build-board.js from the break before sector 2 on, 'hold' (KEEP HOLDING) and 'harness' (sectorContinue() with no argument) pass it by. The card: plain DOM in the debrief's phosphor (styles.css .build-board), COMMS · ISAO, the line 'I can build two of these before the next sector. Choose.', the bank left, a tile per offer (key, name, price, effect, a kind swatch), 1-6 toggle, ENTER or ORDER pays and places, Esc or SKIP takes none, the board owns the keyboard while up and ends a live cut when it opens (a print close-up begun before the debrief ate its keys in the first --board run). Offers (src/domain/build-board.js boardOffers, src/content/build-board.js BUILD_BOARD): the board steps not standing nor bought whose when holds in the coming sector (idle aside, manned kept: the launcher waits for SOL's two passes), at most four; two sentry kinds (the cheapest unlocked, the dearest the bank buys) at the radial's prices when a plan socket is free, Isao ordering it on the emptiest lane's socket (emptiestLaneSite over story.socketToward); the weakest sentry's upgrade; hull repair (dents), spare hull (a hull short), shield rack (not full); a companion whose unit has stream A's `offer` and is unborn (printPet = petPrint.force); a board still short of six fills with the other sentry kinds and the next weakest upgrade. pickable/toggle: two at most, the second re-checked against the bank after the first. src/domain/build-programme.js: `board: true` on board, garage, armory, farm, chips, launcher (src/content/base-programme.js); buy(st, id); due() skips an unbought board step without blocking the steps behind it; snapshot.owed leaves unbought board steps out (the door's 'everything unlocked' rule no longer waits on them) and lists bought. A skipped opening (?skip=defence&sector=N) buys the board steps whose sector gate N reached (jumpBought), so the jump suites print what they printed. The director board (src/domain/director-board.js) moves the six into a BUILD BOARD lane, 'offered from sector n', priced. td-tab 5,357 -> 5,351 (the board's three-line literal paid by the garrison wrapper on one line; the interlude, harness and state hookups on existing lines).
outcome: Ledger on the base (9f0eab02 + the instrumentation, a skipped opening, every body killed every 2 s and paid as the tank's kill, the streak at its cap; artifacts ledger-before.json): income by sector 11,376 / 25,296 / 70,039 / 61,346 / 77,634 kg (kill pay 11,296 / 25,206 / 69,939 / 61,236 / 77,514 from 466 / 826 / 2,070 / 2,522 / 3,534 kills, 22-34 kg a kill; held pay 80-120; the farm 40), nothing spent, bank at each sector's end 11,996 / 37,292 / 107,331 / 168,717 / 246,391; the bank could buy the cheapest sentry 100 % of the fighting samples. With nobody killing (the first, aborted run) sector 1 paid 80 kg held and the bank stood at 700. The finding: since the Pearl crowds, kill pay is 20-100x every price in the game (sentries 45-260, plasma 3 kg/s, the farm's 40); the design's starting table (48-400) would be noise. Prices re-based: the reference player is half the ceiling (the towers', gunship's and SOL's kills pay 0.5); structures board 1,500, garage 2,500, armory 3,200, farm 3,200, chips 2,800, launcher 4,000; repair 1,200, spare 4,800, shield 3,000, a companion 1,800; times a per-sector index [1, 2.2, 5.5, 6, 7] for the board before sectors 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+ (the measured income of the sector before, smoothed); a short board fills with the other sentry kinds and the next upgrade (539e2f7e). Commits 805d4244 (the ledger), 4a743e5e (the board), 539e2f7e (the fill); sentry and upgrade cards at the radial's prices. After (BOARD=pick: the board's own cards first, cheapest first): ceiling 11,996 / 31,092 / 94,046 / 139,956 / 217,456; the reference player (PAY=tower) 6,654 / 13,555 / 42,369 / 59,212 / 100,325, its boards taking shield + armory (6,200 of 6,654), farm + Rotor (7,085 of 13,555), chips + an upgrade (15,431 of 42,369), a Rotor + an upgrade (99 of 59,212). Slightly constrained at the boards before sectors 2 and 3, not after: the income outruns the index and by sector 5 nothing structural is left to buy.
alternatives: Cut the story's kill pay instead (about 1/20, economy plan lever 1 taken far): the design's 48-400 table, the radial's sentries and the plasma's 3 kg/s would mean something again, and 'less than two sentries' worth banked' becomes reachable; not taken unattended because it re-tunes the whole game (the gunship call meter feeds on kill kg, the plasma, the records): the owner's one line, and the index would then go.
A flat price table re-based once: by the board before sector 4 the bank is 6x the sector-2 bank and every card is trivial.
Prices as a share of the bank: always 'affordable at a fraction', a richer player paying more; rejected.

The jump leaves everything to the boards (nothing bought on ?skip=defence): --colony, --round10, --finale and every suite that waits on the board, garage or armory print would need picks first; the jump stands in for the boards before it instead.
Pay at each toggle: a pick taken back would refund; paying at ORDER is the same 'paid at the pick' with no refund path.
Six cards in strict priority with no cap on structures: a skipped board or two would make a board of six structures and no sentry, upgrade or hull card; structures capped at four.
evidence: npm test (322 programs, new test/build-board.mjs: the pool by sector and standing structures, six max, no duplicates, the spine never offered, the price index, the pick of two, the bought gate on due, the jump's purchases, the emptiest lane's socket, the card over a fake DOM: keys, ORDER pays and lets the sector go, Escape takes none), npm run check, npm run architecture, test/host-contracts (78 factories), npm run build green before each commit; test/build-programme (bought in the snapshot), test/director-board (ten prints, six on the board, priced, launcher at s:4), test/ending-host (the interlude left it) updated.

Browser on port 18182 under the lock, from APFS-clone snapshots: --ledger before and after (scratch r6-economy/ledger-before.log, ledger-after-tank.log, ledger-after-tower.log and the JSONs); --board PASS (bank 11,612 at the board before sector 2; ARMORY 3,200 · ROTOR 45 · MORTAR 110 · SHIELD 3,000; keys 1 and 2 picked, the third refused; ENTER paid 3,245 and sector 2 began; Isao printed the armory; the harness continue opened no board), the first two --board runs red on my own bugs (story.sockets is an empty set: the plan's mounts are story.socketToward; a live print cut ate the keys); --director PASS (the BUILD BOARD lane draws six). On the stream's tree: --pearl-story PASS; --pacing PASS (sector 1 first contact 12.5 s, sector 2 20.7 s; the harness continue passes the board); --story-world PASS; --phone PASS with a new phone-board frame (the board at 390 px, then SKIP); --grow red at 'Isao said gunship_overhead' after grow-settled, the same base red the spec names (its owed assertion now expects [] and is past that point).

Open: the sector report's `spent` misses the board's spend (it happens in the break, outside the sector's stats); new lines are unvoiced (the card carries Isao's line, ORDERED is a callout); the cat's card waits for stream A's `offer` field ({ price, fromSector, effect } assumed).
